topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students, sets the scope of the lecture, and introduces the focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of pathogens and tissue damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects infections and cellular damage using molecular patterns, pattern recognition receptors, and downstream signaling complexes.

topics.label: Cellular activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell extravasation, lymphatic migration, and systemic physiological reactions such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms involved in resolving inflammation, repairing damaged tissue, and sustaining chronic inflammatory states such as granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on complement.
